_note: Orbit's station. Rooms have compass exits (n, ne, e, se, s, sw, w, nw, u, d); an exit may be {"to": room, "lock": crew|tech|officer|brass, "oneway": true, "via": lift|ladder|slide|airlock|door, "msg": {en}}. Flags: dark (a headlamp shows it), airless (an EVA suit only), private, landmark (anyone can ask the way there), secret, market ({buys, sells}: kinds of goods or goods; a factor, prices for single goods, about; a good is traded at one market on each world), shop, farm, mine, salvage, rescue (where the air rescue drops you), venue (a place for ceremonies), temple. A room's floor (metal unless said: carpet, grass, stone, rock, suit, wet) and acoustics (room unless said: small, hall, hangar, outside, cave, open) tell the client which footsteps and echo to play. See README.md. Every text is English, {"en": ...}: Orbit is played in English.

about.en: command and science
the Promenade, shops, the Cantina and the crew cabins
Engineering, the Cargo Bay and the Dock
vacuum: an EVA suit only
a mining platform on a tumbling asteroid
shops and the Food Court, a lift up from the Upper Deck
the spaceport, the exchange, the helium tunnels
vacuum: an EVA suit only
domes, a market and the colonists' homes
air too thin to breathe: an EVA suit only
a research station on an ice moon
deadly cold: an EVA suit only
a market inside a tumbling asteroid
woods, a village and a castle
neon streets, a night market and a racing track
a world of arcade halls

desc.en: The docking ring hums with pumps and clamps. Through a thick window you can see the cargo shuttle Dove latched on, its belly scorched from the last reentry. A schedule board lists flights to Moon Base Tranquility. In the next berth, the little mining shuttle Wombat ferries miners to the Asteroid Belt, and north, the Mineral Exchange buys what they bring back.

pilot.en: Pilots: type work to fly a cargo run to the Moon.

all.en: Type ride the Wombat for the shuttle to the Asteroid Belt, or ferry to and a world (the Moon, Karmina...) for the slow public ferry. Your own ship waits in the Hangar, west.

desc.en: The Dove is a stubby cargo shuttle with a white dove painted on its nose. Someone has stuck a sticker on the hatch: "Station, Moon, Station, twice a day".
Cargo runs to Moon Base Tranquility leave whenever a pilot is ready. Round trip: about a minute, thanks to the station's very generous physics.
Beyond the Dove, the black of space and a thin blue line: Earth's atmosphere, seen edge-on.
The Wombat is barely bigger than a minibus, painted green with a wombat on its tail. A sign by its hatch: fare 5 credits, pilots ride free.
A huge hold stacked with containers, strapped down so nothing drifts. A forklift drone beeps as it works, and the air smells of metal and cold: the Ice Depot is just north.
Containers from Earth, the Moon and one from "unknown". That one hums faintly. Best not to ask.
The drone's name, painted on its side, is Humphrey. It beeps politely when it passes you.

security.en: Security: type work to patrol for smugglers.

about.en: ores and meteorites

desc.en: A trading floor just off the Dock, loud with miners back from the Belt. Scales are bolted to the deck, and a price board clatters every time a number changes. At the back, a collector turns a meteorite shard under a lamp, looking for the glitter.

all.en: Ores and meteorites are bought and sold here: type prices, then buy or sell.

desc.en: Iron, nickel, titanium, platinum, quantum crystals, meteorites, rust salt and ember crystals, each with its price flicking up and down. Type prices to hear them.
Heavy scales, checked every morning by an inspector with a very small hammer.

about.en: comet ice, helium-3 and frost pearls

desc.en: A cold hall of insulated tanks and humming chillers, north of the Cargo Bay. Blocks of comet ice, the station's drinking water, wait in frosted crates, beside racks of helium-3 canisters and a small locked case of frost pearls. Your breath clouds in the air.

all.en: Comet ice, helium-3 and frost pearls are bought and sold here: type prices, then buy or sell.

desc.en: Every drop the station drinks passes through these tanks, melted from comet ice and filtered three times. A sign says: please do not lick the pipes.
Frost pearls from Glasir's ice fields, kept cold so they don't cloud. Type prices.
A wide corridor of bare metal lit by caged lamps. Cable trays run along the ceiling, and a maintenance door with a keycard reader stands in the southwest corner.
Colour-coded, mostly. The purple ones don't match any chart.
It needs a crew keycard. Beyond it lie the maintenance tunnels: dark, damp and full of shortcuts.
A plain steel lobby with scuffed floors. Yellow hazard stripes frame the lift doors, and the air smells of machine oil.

Mall Ring, at the top: Gearworks, Orbit Outfitters, Cosy Corner, Whiskers & Widgets, Second Orbit and the Food Court. Upper Deck: the Bridge, the Observation Deck, the Science Lab, Communications and the Archive. Main Deck: the Promenade, the Sky Park, the Cantina, Star Supply, the Medbay, Hydroponics and the crew cabins. Lower Deck: Engineering, the Workshop, the Cargo Bay, the Dock and the Airlock.
A glass lift. Type up or down to ride it.
Painted by hand, slightly wobbly. Someone has signed the corner: Humphrey's cousin.
Hot and loud. The fusion reactor thrums behind a blast window, pipes sing as coolant rushes through, and a repair console blinks amber.

engineer.en: Engineers: type work to repair the reactor.

desc.en: A ball of light the size of a watermelon, held in magnetic fields. When it drifts out of tune, an engineer has to repeat the stabiliser tones.
Four big buttons, numbered one to four, each with its own tone. Low on the left, high on the right.
The pipes are warm to the touch and hum a low note, like a cat purring.

engineer.en: Engineers: repairs here pay a quarter more, with one tone more to repeat.

desc.en: Heat presses on your face. Behind layers of shielding, the fusion core glows like a small, angry sun, and the floor trembles with its hum.
Don't stare. The shielding is good, but you'll still see spots for a minute.

about.en: salvage and memory chips

desc.en: Lathes, welding torches and a pegboard of tools. A half-built robot dog sits on the workbench, waiting patiently for its other two legs. By the door, the engineers' parts counter buys salvage and sells tested memory chips.

all.en: Salvage and memory chips are bought and sold at the parts counter: type prices, then buy or sell.

desc.en: Bins of scrap metal, old circuit boards, satellite chips and a thin stack of gold foil, and a tray of memory chips, each with a green tested sticker. Type prices.
Its tail wags when you look at it. The tail is the only part that's finished.
Every tool has its outline painted behind it. The hammer's outline is empty.
A narrow chamber between two heavy doors, with hooks for spacesuits. A lamp over the outer door glows green: outside, you'll need an EVA suit on.
Green means the outer door may open. Red means someone is still outside. Blinking means somebody pressed it for fun.
Pipes crowd the low ceiling and drip into puddles. The arrows painted on the walls have faded past reading, and a ladder climbs to a hatch above.
Warm water, slightly rusty. The drips keep a steady beat: plink, plink, plonk.
A cramped tunnel where you have to stoop. Something small skitters away from your light: probably just a cleaning bot.
It hides behind a pipe and pretends to be a pipe.
Huge old pumps stand silent, retired long ago. In the south wall there's a small round door with a brass keyhole.
An old-fashioned keyhole: no card reader will open this door, only a real brass key.

all.en: Type open capsule.

desc.en: A tiny round room nobody has entered for years. Letters from the station's first crew are pinned to the walls, and a sealed capsule rests on a pedestal.
One reads: 'To whoever finds this: we built this place so nobody would feel far from home. Look after each other.'
Sealed with wax and a ribbon. It seems to want to be opened, once, by each visitor.
The busiest lift on the station. Travellers with bags wait by the glass doors while a busker plays a soft waltz on a ukulele.

Mall Ring, at the top: Gearworks, Orbit Outfitters, Cosy Corner, Whiskers & Widgets, Second Orbit and the Food Court. Upper Deck: the Bridge, the Observation Deck, the Science Lab, Communications and the Archive. Main Deck: the Promenade, the Sky Park, the Cantina, Star Supply, the Medbay, Hydroponics and the crew cabins. Lower Deck: Engineering, the Workshop, the Cargo Bay, the Dock and the Airlock.
A glass lift. Type up or down to ride it.
He nods at you without missing a note. His hat holds three credits and a button.

The station's main street curves away in both directions, lined with little shops and warm lights. A signpost in the middle points the way to the station's markets, and the mission board glows by the lift. You can smell coffee from the Cantina.

all.en: Look at the signpost for the way to the markets, or type missions for the mission board.

desc.en: The mission board: small jobs around the station, new every day. Type missions to read it.
The Main Lift Lobby is just to the south.

msg.en: Wheee! You spin down the spiral slide and tumble out into {place}.

desc.en: A small park under a painted sky. A mango tree grows in a round bed with benches around it, and a children's spiral slide disappears into the floor.
A sign hangs from a branch: Mangoes belong to everyone. Take one, leave a smile.
A sign says: Lower Deck, one way! Type down to slide.
Warm from the grow lights. A good place to sit and chat.
The quieter end of the Promenade: a barber with one chair, a shop selling cases for phones nobody owns any more, and the smell of coffee from the Cantina.
The barber offers zero-gravity haircuts. The hair floats off; he catches it with a little vacuum.
Round tables bolted to the floor, a long bar that makes the best iced coffee in low Earth orbit, and a jukebox that only plays swing and synthwave. It's the place to sit down and chat.
Behind the bar, a robot barista with one squeaky wheel pours iced coffee into cups with lids, so nothing floats away.
Two buttons: SWING and SYNTHWAVE. Someone has scratched a third one: BOTH.
Iced coffee with milk, instant noodles, fried rice in a pouch, and "Orbit Special": nobody knows what it is.

all.en: The bar sells iced coffee and snacks: type list.
Type casino for the games and their rules. Credits here are only for playing: no real money.

desc.en: A dim, carpeted corner behind the Cantina, all soft lights and chiming machines: a dice table, a row of slot machines, a card table with a robot dealer in a waistcoat, and a lottery booth.
The dealer shuffles with a soft whirr and wishes everyone luck in the same calm voice.
Six machines with pictures of stars, moons, comets, planets, rockets and one golden ring called the Orbit.
Tickets for this week's draw, every Sunday at 12:00 station time. Type lottery.
Rows of lettuce, chillies and tomatoes grow under pink lights, and water trickles through clear tubes. It smells like rain here. Crates of fresh vegetables wait by the door.
The chillies are the station's pride: small, red and dangerously hot. Somebody has labelled one row "for chilli sauce only".
Crates of fresh vegetables, ready for delivery. Take them only when a mission asks for them.
Paper packets of seeds, from quick water spinach to slow and precious moon melons. Type list to see them.

all.en: Type plots to see your plots, plant tomato to plant, harvest when it's ripe, and list for seeds. The Spice Market, west, buys what you grow.

about.en: coffee, spices and crops

desc.en: A covered market that smells of roasting coffee, cloves and cardamom. Stallholders scoop coffee beans into sacks and spices into jars, and the farmers from Hydroponics, next door, sell their crops by the crate: water spinach, chillies, strawberries, and now and then a moon melon.

all.en: Coffee, spices and crops are bought and sold here: type prices, then buy or sell.

desc.en: Sacks of coffee from the hills of Earth, jars of cloves, nutmeg and cinnamon, and crates of whatever Hydroponics grew this week. Type prices.
A copper drum turns slowly over a heating coil, and the beans inside crackle. The smell reaches the Promenade on a good day.

A white pavilion of carved wood stands among beds of jasmine and orchids, its roof hung with strings of tiny flowers. A shallow pool reflects the lantern light, and a path of smooth stones leads to a raised floor where two people could stand face to face. The air is sweet and still.
Strings of jasmine buds, threaded by hand every morning by the garden crew. They open slowly as the day goes on.
Still water with a few floating petals. If you're quiet, you can hear it lapping at the stones.
Brighter and busier than the west end: shop windows glow, a noodle cart steams, and a holographic sign flickers with today's specials.
Chicken noodles, in a bowl with a lid. The owner swears the lid is for your safety.
Today's specials: everything is special. The sign is very proud of itself.

all.en: Type list to see what's for sale, and buy to buy.

desc.en: A crowded general store: shelves of gadgets, seed packets, tools, clothes and oddities. The shopkeeper, a cheerful robot in a bow tie, rolls over to greet you.
Its name tag says TOBY. It says 'Welcome, valued customer!' to everyone, including the door.
Everything a spacefarer might need, and a few things nobody needs, like a snow globe with the Moon inside.

all.en: The family desk is here: type adopt to give a little one a home.

desc.en: Clean, white and quiet, apart from the patient beep of a heart monitor. A medkit cabinet hangs on the wall next to two neatly made beds, and a small desk with a vase of paper stars stands by the door to the nursery.
Rows of medkits with the station's logo, a planet with a ring. Missions sometimes need one delivered.
Two beds with straps, so patients don't float off in their sleep.

The family desk. Little ones who arrived in the simulation without a family are cared for in the nursery behind it, until someone gives them a home. Type adopt: partners decide together, and anyone of level 3 or more may.

Padded walls, dumbbells floating on elastic cords, and a treadmill with a harness. It smells of rubber and determination. A ring painted on the padded floor is for duels: challenge someone here with duel and their name.
You have to strap in, or you'll jog straight into the ceiling.
They weigh nothing up here, which is somehow harder.
A long carpeted hallway lined with numbered doors. Someone has strung fairy lights along the ceiling, and a maintenance hatch is set into the floor.
Your own door is the one to the south: it opens only for you, and for guests you invite.
A crew keycard reader blinks beside it. Below, the maintenance tunnels are dark.
Every third bulb is a different colour. It's cheerful, like a wedding next door.
Your own small cabin: a bunk with a blanket from home, a round window full of stars, and a shelf for your things. It's quiet here, and nobody comes in unless you invite them.
The blanket from home still smells a little of the laundry soap your family uses.
Stars, more than you have ever seen at once, and none of them twinkle up here.
A shelf with a net over it, so your things stay put.
A round lobby with a glass lift in the middle and a thick blue carpet. A brass plaque by the lift lists the decks.

Mall Ring, at the top: Gearworks, Orbit Outfitters, Cosy Corner, Whiskers & Widgets, Second Orbit and the Food Court. Upper Deck: the Bridge, the Observation Deck, the Science Lab, Communications and the Archive. Main Deck: the Promenade, the Sky Park, the Cantina, Star Supply, the Medbay, Hydroponics and the crew cabins. Lower Deck: Engineering, the Workshop, the Cargo Bay, the Dock and the Airlock.
A glass lift. Type up or down to ride it.
A hushed corridor with portraits of past captains along the walls. Officers hurry by with tablets, talking in low voices.
Eleven captains, from a stern woman with a monocle to a young man grinning with a pineapple in his hands.
The captain's chair faces a wall of displays: the station's orbit, shuttle traffic and the health of every system. Officers talk in low voices over their consoles.
Leather, worn, with a cup holder that has seen a lot of coffee. Sitting in it is strictly forbidden, and very tempting.
The main display draws the station's orbit as a green ring around Earth: one lap every 92 minutes.
Wood panels, a smell of cloves, and a model of the station hanging from the ceiling. An old guitar leans against a sea chest with a padlock.
Every window of the model is lit, and one tiny figure waves from the Observation Deck.
Three strings left. A sticker on it says: play me only at dawn.
Radios crackle with chatter from Earth and the Moon. A wall of dials glows green, and a spare headset hangs on a hook by the door.
Mostly weather reports, and a ground station on a small island asking whether anyone has seen their cat.
Every dial points at a satellite. One is labelled in marker pen: do not touch, seriously.
A dome of thick glass, dimmed so your eyes can see outside. Earth fills half the sky.
An old brass telescope, bolted to the rail. Someone has pointed it at the Moon and taped a note to it: "hi mum".
Shelves of glowing data crystals hum softly in the dim light. A librarian robot dusts them carefully, although there is no dust in space.
Logs of every day on the station since it was built. The oldest crystal flickers, as if tired.
It whispers 'shh' at you, then at itself.

scientist.en: Scientists: type work to analyse samples.

desc.en: Benches crowded with microscopes, a centrifuge whirring in the corner, and a whiteboard full of equations with one doodle of a cat.
The analyser prints a row of readings and waits for someone clever to work out the next one.
The cat has been given a name: Schrodinger Junior.

all.en: Here you can ring the bell, read the plaque, or light a lantern for 3 credits.

desc.en: A round hall under a great dome of glass, so clear that the stars seem close enough to touch. Rows of pale wooden benches face a small raised floor, soft light glows from lanterns in an alcove, and a bronze bell hangs from a slender arch. This is the temple of the Way of Starlight, and people speak in whispers here.
A bell of dark bronze with three rings cast around its rim. Struck once, it answers with three soft tones, low, middle and high, that drift from one side of the dome to the other. Type ring bell.
Small paper lanterns in the shape of stars, each lit by someone for a promise they mean to keep. Type light lantern to light one of your own.

THE WAY OF STARLIGHT. Long before this station was built, the first explorers crossed the dark between worlds with nothing to steer by but the stars. On the longest crossing, when their instruments failed, they made each other a promise: to keep watch in turns, to share what they had, and never to leave anyone behind. They spoke the words aloud under the open sky, and every one of them came home. Ever since, travellers have held that a promise spoken under the stars is kept by their light, and that the light is kept by those who keep their promises. The Way asks only three things: keep your word, stay curious, and look after one another. Light a lantern for a promise, and ring the bell for those who are travelling still.
Smooth pale wood, worn soft by many quiet visitors.
The glass is so clear you forget it's there. The Milky Way arches overhead like a river of light.
You clip your tether to a rail on the station's skin. Everything is silent except your own breathing, and Earth turns slowly beneath your boots.
Scuffed by a thousand gloves. Somebody has scratched a heart into it.
Rows of dark blue panels stretch away like a field of glass, all turned to follow the sun.
A small bird-shaped sticker sits on one panel. It must have been put there by someone very tall and very brave.
A tall mast bristling with dishes. Your helmet radio catches a faint crackle of music from somewhere very far away.
They all point at Earth except one, which points at nothing at all.

all.en: Type collect to salvage.

desc.en: A tangle of old satellite scraps caught in the station's nets. Most of it is junk, but here and there something glitters.
Strong enough to catch a bus. Over the years they've caught a boot, a spanner and a rubber duck.

all.en: Type mine to mine. The Wombat flies you back when you type ride the Wombat.

desc.en: A pressurised dome bolted onto a tumbling asteroid. Drills and ore carts line the walls, and pebbles tick against the glass.
An old miner buys ore here for three quarters of the station market's price. Type sell to deal with her.
The Wombat waits by the dome's hatch, its engines ticking as they cool.
Grey rock under a black sky, cratered and utterly silent. Veins of metal glint where the dust has been brushed away.
Richer than inside the dome. Miners come out here for the good stuff, and keep an eye on their air.
A narrow cave deep inside the asteroid. When your light touches the walls, crystals flash back in blue and violet.
Some of them hum when you tap them, a note so low you feel it in your teeth.
The cockpit of the cargo shuttle Dove. The autopilot hums, and the Moon grows slowly in the window.
The little mining shuttle Wombat hums through the dark, its windows full of tumbling rocks.
The lift opens onto polished white floors and soft music. A banner hangs overhead: Welcome to the Mall Ring, open every hour of every day.
Under the welcome, smaller letters: shoplifting is pointless in a closed space station.
Type down to go back to the Upper Deck.
A bright, round hall at the heart of the Mall Ring. A fountain of floating water droplets turns slowly in the middle, and a glowing directory lists the shops.
Each droplet is the size of a marble. Children try to catch them; the droplets always win.
West: Gearworks, Orbit Outfitters and Second Orbit (a pawn shop). East: Cosy Corner, Whiskers & Widgets and Starglint Jewellers, with the wedding desk. North: the Food Court.

all.en: Food here gives little boosts. Type list to see what's for sale, and buy to buy.

desc.en: Long tables with magnetic trays, and counters selling iced coffee, stuffed pancakes and crackers in sealed bags. Somebody's birthday song drifts from a corner table.
Every counter has a small robot cook with a very serious face.
A gently curving walkway of shop fronts: tools to the west, clothes to the north, and a cluttered secondhand shop to the south.
One window shows a mannequin in an EVA suit, posed as if it's dancing.

all.en: Devices, keycards, EVA gear and tools. Type list to see what's for sale, and buy to buy.

desc.en: Racks of devices and tools up to the ceiling: mappers, scanners, headlamps, keycards, drills, and a spacesuit on a stand that follows you with its empty helmet.
Every price tag has been hand-written by someone with very neat letters.

all.en: Clothes and titles. Type list to see what's for sale, and buy to buy.

desc.en: Rails of clothes in every colour, a mirror that compliments you, and a counter of engraved name plates for those who want a title.
It says: 'Stunning. Truly. Would you like to try the golden one?'

all.en: Type sell and a thing you own: she pays 40 percent of its price.

desc.en: A narrow shop stuffed with things people didn't need any more. The owner, an old woman with a jeweller's loupe, buys your things for a fraction of their price.
She squints through it at everything, including you.
The quieter half of the Mall Ring: a furniture shop to the east, to the north a shop that chirps, purrs and beeps, and to the northeast a jeweller's window that glitters even with the lights off.
A bench for people waiting for people who are still shopping.

all.en: Furniture for your cabin, seen by the guests you invite. Type list to see what's for sale, and buy to buy.

desc.en: Sofas, rugs, lamps and hammocks arranged like little rooms. It smells of rattan and new cushions.
One of them has a sign: 'Try me'. It's very comfortable.

all.en: Pets looking for a home. Type list to see what's for sale, and buy to buy.

desc.en: Little robots roll between baskets where orange cats sleep in magnetic harnesses. Everything here wants to come home with you.
One cat opens an eye, decides you're acceptable, and closes it again.

all.en: Rings for a proposal, and the wedding desk. Type list to see the rings, and talk to Celeste about weddings.

desc.en: Glass cases of rings sit on deep blue velvet, each one lit by its own tiny lamp. At the back, a writing desk holds a thick leather book of bookings and a vase of fresh jasmine.
Silver bands, gold bands, and a single ring with a crystal that holds a tiny point of starlight.
The wedding desk. Engaged couples book a hall here: book wedding, the hall, the tier, the ceremony and the time. Type wedding schedule for the weddings to come.
A hangar bay of your crew's own, behind a door that opens only for its members. Folding chairs circle a scuffed table, a crew board glows on the wall, and a shelf waits for trophies.

all.en: Only your crew comes in here. Type crew for the crew, and crew say to talk to all of them, wherever they are.

desc.en: The crew board: your crew's points and place among the crews. Type crew for more, and crews for the whole board.
Room for trophies, and a table with a ring from somebody's iced coffee that nobody will admit to.

A tall round hall beside the lifts. In its middle a ring of pale light hangs in the air: the Gate, where the simulation folds space so you can step from one world to another. A board lists the worlds and what the Gate charges to reach each, and the ring hums one low note that seems to come from every direction at once.

all.en: Type worlds to see where the Gate goes, and gate to Karmina (or any world) to step through, for a fee.

desc.en: The worlds and the Gate's fees. Type worlds to hear them.
The ring's light ripples like water when someone steps through, and the air smells faintly of rain.

A long hangar west of the Dock, lined with numbered berths. Players' own ships rest in their docking clamps, fuel lines snaking across the floor to each one, and a tired robot sweeps up after every landing.

all.en: Your own ship waits here: type embark to go aboard (buy one at the Shipyard on the Mall Ring).

desc.en: Numbered berths with heavy clamps, most of them empty, waiting for players' ships.
A tired sweeping robot. It sighs, electronically, every time a ship lands.

A bright showroom with a curved window onto the stars. Four ships turn slowly on pedestals, from a snub-nosed little shuttle to a long explorer with folded solar wings, and a salesman in a silver jacket insists each one is a bargain.

all.en: Type list to see the ships, examine a ship for its cargo hold, speed and fuel tank, and buy one. Your ship waits for you in the Hangar, west of the Dock.

desc.en: Four ships on turning pedestals. Type list to hear their prices, and examine one for its hold, speed and tank.
The salesman's jacket is so shiny you can hear it. He promises a fair trade-in for your old ship.

The spaceport of Moon Base Tranquility: a low grey hall pressed into the lunar soil, its landing pads outside the windows ringed with blue lights. A small copy of the station's Gate shimmers by the arrivals desk, and the ferry's berth waits beside it. You feel lighter here; every step wants to become a hop.

all.en: From here: the Gate home or anywhere (gate to the station), the ferry (ferry to the station), or your own ship (embark).

desc.en: Landing pads ringed with blue lights; now and then a ship settles onto one in a puff of grey dust that takes ages to fall.
Stacks of crates from the station fill the depot: seeds, spare parts, sacks of coffee. This is where the Dove's cargo runs end, and a forklift beeps patiently as it sorts them.
The forklift beeps politely before every turn, even with nobody around.
The base's main corridor, a tube of white panels with signs in six languages. The exchange is to the west, the helium tunnels to the east, and the Earthrise Dome to the north.
Signs in six languages. One of them has a small smiley face drawn on it.
A trading floor under a low dome, its price boards glowing amber. Helium-3 is cheap here, straight from the tunnels; water ice and fresh food are dear, because everything else comes a long way.

all.en: Type prices to hear what sells cheap and dear on the Moon.

desc.en: Amber numbers scroll past. Type prices to hear them.
Pressurised tunnels bored through the regolith, lit by strings of bulbs. Drill rigs chew the grey soil for helium-3, the fuel the whole system runs on, and the walls glitter with glassy beads.

all.en: Type mine for helium-3 and lunar ore.

desc.en: Drill rigs grind the regolith; the glassy beads are old lava, frozen into droplets long ago.
A clear dome over a small garden of lunar ferns. Above the horizon hangs the Earth, blue and white and impossibly bright, never rising and never setting, only turning slowly through its days.
The whole Earth in one glance: swirls of cloud, a blue ocean, and on its night side the lights of cities strung along the coasts like beads.
A cramped airlock with suits on hooks and a scuffed sign: check your air before you step outside. The tow crew brings back anyone whose air runs out, for a fee.
Spare suits for visitors, all a little too big.
A grey plain under a black sky, footprints everywhere and none of them fading. Your suit's hiss is the only sound. A crater rim rises to the east.
With no wind to blow them away, every footprint here will last a million years.
The edge of an old crater, its floor lost in shadow far below. From here the base looks like a handful of pebbles, and the Earth hangs over it like a lantern.
The crater's floor has never seen sunlight. Ice may be hiding down there.

Red dust drifts across the spaceport's windows, and the light outside is the colour of weak tea. Karmina's colonists wave newcomers through with tired smiles. The Gate's ring shines by the customs desk, and the ferry berth is beside it.

all.en: From here: the Gate, the ferry, or your own ship. Water ice sells dear on Karmina.

desc.en: Customs officers in red jackets check arrivals from the Gate and the ferry; ships less often.

The heart of the colony under its biggest dome: a square of red tiles, a fountain that runs only at noon to save water, and children chasing a robot dog. The market is west, the farming domes east, and the habitat ring north.
Dry now. At noon it runs for exactly ten minutes, and everyone comes to watch.
Stalls under striped awnings sell dome-grown red quinoa and jars of rust salt dug from the flats. Everyone here asks the same thing: have you brought any ice?
Red quinoa, rust salt, and a stall selling ice by the cup. Type prices.
Row after row of red quinoa and tomato vines under humming grow lights, the air thick and warm and smelling of wet soil. A sign says: pickers welcome, take a share of what you gather.

all.en: Type collect to pick a share of the harvest.

desc.en: Quinoa heads nod under the lamps like red feathers. Type collect to pick a share.
A circle of family homes built from red bricks pressed out of the planet's own dust, each with a window box of stubborn flowers. The storm shelter is west, the rover garage east.
Marigolds, mostly: tough little flowers that don't mind thin air.
A thick-walled bunker with benches, blankets and a shelf of board games. When the dust storms come, the whole colony crowds in here and tells stories until the sky clears.
Well-worn board games; the chess set is missing a knight, replaced by a bolt.
Six-wheeled rovers sit under tarps, their tyres caked with red dust. An airlock leads out to the Rust Flats; the colonists' tow rover brings back anyone whose air runs out.
Six-wheeled rovers. One has a name painted on its side: Lucky.
An endless plain of red sand under a butterscotch sky. The air is far too thin to breathe. Crusts of rust-coloured salt crack under your boots, and the colonists dig it for the market.

all.en: Type collect to dig rust salt.

desc.en: Rust-coloured salt crusts. Type collect to dig some.
The flats end at a canyon so deep and wide that its far wall is blue with distance. Two small moons hurry across the sky.
Two potato-shaped moons race each other across the sky.

A landing field scraped out of blue-white ice, its terminal a cluster of insulated domes. Frost flowers grow on the inside of every window. The Gate's ring hangs by the heaters, and the ferry docks beside it.

all.en: From here: the Gate, the ferry, or your own ship. Ice is cheap on Glasir; coffee and spices are not.

desc.en: Feathery frost flowers, each one different, grown overnight on the glass.
Scientists in thick jumpers bend over ice cores laid out like strips of glass. Somewhere under the crust, they say, is an ocean. The traders' post is west, the thermal lodge east.
Ice cores with thin dark bands: each band a year of dust, they say.
A warm, crowded hut where blocks of ice are weighed on brass scales and sold by the tonne. A kettle never stops boiling; a cup of real coffee here costs a small fortune.
Brass scales for weighing ice. Type prices.
Pipes of water warmed deep underground run through the floor, and everyone sits with their boots off. An airlock leads out to the quarry; the lodge's tow sled brings back anyone whose air runs out.
The floor is warm enough to fall asleep on, and several people have.

Terraces of blue ice cut into the moon's crust, so cold that it burns through gloves. Without a suit you would freeze in moments. Cutters leave blocks stacked for anyone with a sled, and deeper down a crevasse glows blue.

all.en: Type collect to cut ice (and, now and then, a frost pearl).

desc.en: Blocks of blue ice, stacked for the taking. Type collect.
Every few minutes a plume of vapour shoots from a crack in the ice, climbs higher than the station's tallest deck, and falls back as glittering snow.
A plume rises, hangs glittering, and falls as snow.
A narrow crack deep in the ice. Where your light falls, the walls glow sapphire, and pearls of frozen water hang from ledges like berries.

all.en: Type collect for frost pearls; you'll need light.

desc.en: Frost pearls on the ledges. Type collect.

in.en: at the Drift Bazaar's docking ring

desc.en: A ring of mismatched docking clamps welded to a hollow, tumbling asteroid: the Drift Bazaar. Hawkers shout prices before you are even out of the hatch. Nobody here checks cargo, which is exactly why people come. A patched-up copy of the Gate flickers by the ferry berth.

all.en: No customs at the Drift Bazaar. Other worlds do check what you carry.

desc.en: Hawkers selling everything from spare fuses to fortune-telling robots.

A cavern hollowed out of the rock and packed with stalls lit by paper lanterns and old neon. You can buy almost anything here, and collectors pay well for rare ores and meteorites. Spice Row is west, a cafe east, and the lookout north.
Paper lanterns and old neon, and a thousand voices haggling. Type prices.
A narrow lane where the air is thick with cinnamon, clove and pepper. Sacks of spices are piled to the ceiling, cheaper here than anywhere else. A dim alley leads south, and nobody looks at it.
Sacks of cinnamon, clove, nutmeg and pepper, cheapest here of anywhere.

A dead end between two stalls, where a woman in a long coat sells things with no labels: star orchids that are forbidden to pick, chips that nobody registered. Neon City pays a fortune for them, if the customs officers on your way don't find them first.

all.en: Contraband: cheap here, dear in Lumina City. Customs on the station, the Moon, Karmina, Glasir and in Lumina may take it, and fine you.

desc.en: Two stalls with their shutters half down, and crates with no labels stacked behind them. Type prices to hear what's for sale, or talk to Shade.
A cafe whose tables are bolted to the floor because the whole asteroid wobbles. Traders swap rumours about prices over cups of ginger tea.
Ginger tea in cups with weighted bottoms, so they don't wander off.
A bubble of thick glass on the asteroid's skin. The stars wheel past as the rock tumbles, and sometimes a trader's ship slides by close enough to wave at.
The stars wheel round once every few minutes as the asteroid tumbles.

A wooden pier that juts out over nothing at all, where ships of the simulation tie up beside sailing boats with cloth wings. Beyond it lies Evergrove, a world of old forests and older stories. The Gate here is a circle of standing stones humming with light.

all.en: Small creatures live in Evergrove's woods: type face and a creature's name to test your wits against it. Nobody gets hurt.

desc.en: The standing stones hum when the Gate opens; the boats' cloth wings flap lazily.

Cottages with turf roofs gather around a well, and a market cart sells moonpetals by the basket. The villagers pay good coin for spices and coffee, which they call sailors' magic. The woods are west, a mushroom hollow east, and the castle north.
The well is wishing-well deep. The market cart sells moonpetals: type prices.
Tall trees lean together and murmur in a wind you cannot feel. Moss sprites, no bigger than a thumb, dart between the ferns and giggle at travellers.
Tall murmuring trees. Moss sprites hide in the ferns: face moss sprite.
So dark under the canopy that the only light comes from beetles glowing like embers. Something large and furry snores in a thicket.
Something big snores in the thicket. Ember beetles glow on the branches.
A dell of giant mushrooms, red with white spots, some big enough to shelter under. Puffcap imps bounce on the caps and challenge anyone who passes to a riddle.
Mushroom caps as big as umbrellas; the imps bounce on them like drums.
A drawbridge over a moat of lilies, guarded by a stone knight who bows to everyone. The castle's banners show a silver acorn on green.
The stone knight bows with a grinding noise, and says good day in both languages.
Long tables, a fire big enough to roast a cart, and tapestries of dragons that turn out, on closer look, to be very large lizards having a nap. A spiral stair climbs to the tower.
Dragons, or large napping lizards; opinions differ.

in.en: at the top of the Star Tower

desc.en: The tower's top is open to the sky, where the simulation's stars are painted a little too bright. From here the whole of Evergrove spreads out like a quilt.
Look closely and a few stars blink in a pattern, as if someone is signalling.

A landing deck on top of a skyscraper, slick with rain that never stops. Below, Lumina City glows in every colour a sign can be. City police drones hover by the arrivals gate and scan the odd traveller; the Gate's ring here is pink neon.

all.en: The Courier Hub hires anyone: type gig there. The Night Market pays dear for what the Drift Bazaar sells in its back alley.

desc.en: City drones with polite voices and very good scanners.

A wide street under a canopy of holograms: noodle stalls, hovercabs, a giant koi fish made of light swimming between the towers. The Night Market is west, the Courier Hub east, the Hologram Plaza north.
A koi of light, as long as a ferry, swimming slowly between the towers.
Stalls under tarps sell circuit boards by the kilo and chips cheaper than anywhere in the system. Some sellers lower their voices and ask whether you've come from the Drift Bazaar.
Circuit boards by the kilo, chips by the handful. Type prices.
Water drips from a hundred air conditioners into puddles that reflect the signs upside down. A cat made of hologram static watches you from a fire escape.
The hologram cat flickers, yawns, and ignores you completely.
A garage full of parcels and scooters, run by a dispatcher who talks to six people at once. There is always something that needs to be somewhere else in a hurry.

all.en: Type gig for a delivery: carry the parcel to the room it names before the time runs out.

desc.en: Stacks of parcels, each with a glowing address. Type gig to take one.
A glowing ribbon of track loops between the towers, and hover bikes scream round it in streaks of light. The grandstand smells of rain and hot metal.
Hover bikes scream past in streaks of light. The races are coming soon.
A square where giant holograms of dancers loop above the crowd. A lift climbs to the Sky Bar, and an apartment tower's lobby opens to the east.
Giant hologram dancers, looping the same eight steps forever.
A glass bar at the top of the tallest tower, where the rain falls past the windows instead of on you. The city spreads below like spilled jewellery.
The whole city, glittering, and the rain sliding down the glass.
A marble lobby with a doorman robot who remembers everyone's birthday, and a wall of letterboxes that the couriers keep busy.
The doorman robot wishes you a happy birthday, just in case.
A boardwalk made of big square pixels that chime softly when you step on them, stretching over a sea of scrolling stars. A blocky Gate ring blinks by the ferry berth.
Each pixel chimes a different note; walking plays a tune.
A hall of flashing cabinets, carpet printed with little planets, and the endless music of a hundred games at once. Cabinet Row is west, the prize counter east, the tournament stage north.
A hundred games, all playing their music at once.

A long row of game cabinets humming and blinking. Four of them are lit and waiting: Quick Draw, Star Beat, Echo and Meteor Dodge. A token machine by the wall sells tokens, and each cabinet prints prize tickets when you do well.
Four lit cabinets.
Shelves of plush comets, glow stars and little arcade cabinets, and a single enormous robot that nobody has ever won. The counter takes prize tickets: list shows what they buy.
The enormous robot prize waves at you. Nobody has ever won it.
A stage under spotlights with two big chairs facing a giant screen, where players settle quick-draw duels: duel and a name. The high score wall glows to the east.
The giant screen shows a countdown that never seems to reach zero.
A wall of glowing initials and numbers, every one of them a boast: the best at each cabinet. Look at the wall to read it.
Empty lines at the top, waiting for someone's initials.
A long cabin of worn blue seats, a vending machine that only sells ginger sweets, and a window where the stars crawl past. The ferry is slow, but it gets everyone there in the end.
A snug cabin with a cockpit at its nose: two seats, a panel of dials, and a window full of stars.

en.you: You dance, a little clumsily in low gravity.
en.they: {actor} dances, a little clumsily in low gravity.

day.en: green islands scattered across a turquoise sea

night.en: Java's lights glitter like a string of gold, with Jakarta the brightest bead

day.en: a scatter of islands under puffy clouds
green hills and the brown ribbon of the Mekong

night.en: Bangkok and Kuala Lumpur shine like coins on black velvet

day.en: the red heart of the desert, ringed by blue

night.en: dark almost everywhere, with a few bright cities along the coast

day.en: a green arc of islands with snowy mountains

night.en: Tokyo spills light across the whole bay

day.en: mountains, rivers and the pale Gobi desert

night.en: a web of city lights spreads along the coast

day.en: the snow of the Himalaya to the north, green plains below it

night.en: thousands of towns sparkle like spilled sugar

day.en: gold and orange sand from edge to edge

night.en: Dubai burns bright on the Gulf's shore

day.en: a patchwork of green fields under drifting clouds

night.en: cities glow everywhere, joined by threads of motorway

day.en: endless dark forest and winding rivers

night.en: almost completely dark, with a lonely town here and there

day.en: the orange Sahara in the north and the deep green of the Congo

night.en: mostly dark, with the Nile a thin thread of light

day.en: prairies, mountains and the Great Lakes shining like mirrors

night.en: a glittering grid of cities from coast to coast

day.en: the green ocean of the Amazon, and the Andes like a spine

night.en: São Paulo and Buenos Aires shine brightest

day.en: blinding white ice as far as you can see

night.en: and maybe, if you're lucky, a green curtain of aurora

day.en: deep blue water with a few tiny islands

night.en: black water, and not a single light

day.en: blue water streaked with long white clouds

night.en: dark water, a ship's light here and there

day.en: turquoise water and towering storm clouds

night.en: dark water, with lightning flickering inside the clouds
cold, dark water under the southern stars

day.en: a cracked white lid of sea ice

night.en: darkness, and sometimes an aurora dancing

about.en: the hub where everyone comes into the simulation
mining on a tumbling rock (the Wombat flies there from the Dock)
helium-3 cheap, ice and fresh food dear
the neon city: chips cheap, helium-3 and rare goods dear
the arcade world: four cabinet games, prizes and high scores
the fantasy world: moonpetals cheap, spices and coffee dear
the red planet: water ice sells dear, red quinoa and rust salt cheap
the asteroid market: spices cheap, rare ores dear, and no customs
the ice moon: ice and frost pearls cheap, coffee and spices dear
collect meteorites at the Observation Deck, on the hull walk or on the Moon's Sea of Dust

start.en: A meteor shower is sweeping past the station! Fragments are raining onto the hull walk and past the Observation Deck, and onto the Moon's Sea of Dust. Type collect there to gather them.

end.en: The meteor shower has passed.

found.en: You catch {things} as it tumbles past!

about.en: engineers earn half again for repairs while it lasts

start.en: Solar storm! The lights flicker and the reactor strains. Engineers: every repair pays half again until it passes.

end.en: The solar storm has passed, and the lights are steady again.

about.en: collect the loose crates in the Cargo Bay

start.en: Crash! A cargo net has snapped in the Cargo Bay, and crates are rolling everywhere. Type collect there: the quartermaster pays for every crate brought back.

end.en: The last crate is back in its net.

found.en: You haul a crate back: the quartermaster pays {n} credits.

about.en: listen for its beeps and catch it in the right room

start.en: A little robot pet has escaped from Whiskers & Widgets and is hiding somewhere on the station! Type listen to hear which way its beeps come from, and catch it when you're in the right room.

end.en: The little robot has gone home by itself.

won.en: {name} caught the runaway robot and wins {n} credits!

about.en: search the rooms for the stowaway (security officers are paid double)

start.en: Stowaway alert! Someone slipped aboard with the last shuttle and is hiding on the station. Type search in a room to look; each search tells you which way the footsteps went.

end.en: The stowaway slipped away on the next shuttle.

won.en: {name} found the stowaway and wins {n} credits!

wrong.en: Nobody here, but you hear footsteps.

about.en: one world pays far more for one kind of goods

start.en: Market news: {place} is short of {kind}! Prices there are up by a third for the next quarter of an hour.

end.en: The market boom is over; prices are settling.

about.en: one world sells one kind of goods cheap

start.en: Market news: {place} has too much {kind}! Prices there are down by a third for the next quarter of an hour: a good time to buy.

end.en: The market has recovered.

about.en: all XP is doubled

start.en: The simulation is feeling generous: for the next hour, everything you do earns double XP!

end.en: Double XP hour is over.

about.en: half price at the Cantina's bar and the Food Court

start.en: Happy hour at the Cantina! For the next half hour, iced coffee and snacks are half price at the bar and the Food Court.

end.en: Happy hour is over. Back to full price.

about.en: watch it from the Observation Deck, the Earthrise Dome or a lookout

start.en: A comet is passing close by, its tail stretched across half the sky! Type watch at the Observation Deck, the Moon's Earthrise Dome, Evergrove's Star Tower or the Bazaar's lookout.

end.en: The comet has gone on its way.

seen.en: You watch the comet's long, glowing tail drift across the stars. Somebody takes a photo and pays you {n} credits for pointing it out.

about.en: some rooms go dark: a headlamp helps

start.en: Power outage! The Lower Deck and the Promenade have gone dark until the engineers fix it. A headlamp helps.

end.en: The power is back on.

about.en: take shelter in Karmina's Storm Shelter for tea and stories

start.en: A dust storm is rolling over Karmina! The colonists are heading for the Storm Shelter, with tea and stories for anyone who joins them there (type join).

end.en: The dust storm on Karmina has blown over.

joined.en: You squeeze onto a bench with the colonists. Someone hands you tea and a blanket; you get {n} credits' worth of hospitality.

about.en: everyone at the Dock fixes it together: type fix drone

start.en: Alert! A giant maintenance drone has malfunctioned and is blundering around the Dock, grabbing crates. Everyone, to the Dock! Type fix drone there to help shut it down; the more who help, the better the reward. Nobody gets hurt.

end.en: The drone got away into the vents. Everyone who tried gets a thank-you.

won.en: The drone powers down with a sad whistle. Well done, everyone! Rewards: {rewards}.

hit.en: You pry open a panel and yank a cable: the drone shudders ({left} to go).

miss.en: The drone swats your hand away. Try again in a moment.

name.en: Trading fair on the Mall Ring

about.en: every shop on the Mall Ring is a fifth off

start.en: The weekly trading fair has opened on the Mall Ring: every shop there is a fifth off for the next two hours!

end.en: The trading fair has closed until next week.

name.en: Jackpot night at the Casino Corner

about.en: three of a kind on the slots pays double

start.en: Jackpot night! For the next two hours, three of a kind on the Casino Corner's slots pays double.

end.en: Jackpot night is over. The slots are back to their usual selves.

about.en: courier gigs in Lumina pay double

start.en: Night rush in Lumina City! For the next two hours, every courier gig pays double.

end.en: The night rush in Lumina is over.

about.en: win duels on the Tournament Stage: the most wins take the prizes

start.en: The duel tournament has begun on Pixel Pier's Tournament Stage! For two hours, every duel won there counts; the most wins take 500, 200 and 100 credits, and the champion a title.

end.en: The duel tournament is over.

about.en: everyone gets a birthday gift: type join

start.en: Happy birthday, Orbit! The station opened on the 25th of September, and today everyone gets a gift: type join to open yours. There's cake in the Cantina.

end.en: The birthday party is over until next year.

joined.en: You open your birthday gift: {n} credits and an iced coffee!

about.en: watch the fireworks from a view

start.en: Happy New Year! Fireworks are blooming over the Earth. Type watch at the Observation Deck, or any lookout, to see them.

end.en: The last fireworks have faded. Here's to a good year.

seen.en: Fireworks burst in silent colour over the Earth's night side. Someone passes round a tray of sweets and a gift of {n} credits.

name.en: The Lantern Festival of the Way of Starlight

about.en: light a lantern in the Star Dome Hall: free today, with a gift, and when enough glow, a gift for everyone

start.en: Today is the Lantern Festival of the Way of Starlight: the hundredth day of the year, when the station fills with small lights. Lanterns in the Star Dome Hall are free today, whoever lights one is thanked with a gift, and when enough of them glow together, everyone on the station shares a gift.

end.en: The Lantern Festival is over; the lanterns glow on until morning.

about.en: visit the host's cabin from the Crew Quarters

start.en: {name} is throwing a party in their cabin! Everyone's welcome for the next half hour: go to the Crew Quarters and type visit {name}.

end.en: {name}'s party is over. Thanks for coming!

about.en: see the message

start.en: {message}
